holidays.name: National Sunglasses Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the coolest eye accessory ever made. Slip on your shades, strike a pose, and pretend you are a movie star or a secret agent, even if you are just going to the grocery store.
holidays.origin: Promoted by The Vision Council in the United States to encourage UV eye protection. It is now celebrated each year on June 27 and has become popular on social media.
holidays.funFact: Sunglasses date back to 12th-century China, where judges wore smoky quartz lenses to hide their facial expressions while questioning witnesses.

holidays.name: National Orange Blossom Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the fragrant white flowers of the orange tree, which are known for their sweet scent and have long been used in perfumes, teas, and weddings.
holidays.origin: The orange blossom is the state flower of Florida, and the day honors the flower's cultural importance. The date was set by fans of the plant, and the day is celebrated informally.
holidays.funFact: Orange blossoms became a wedding tradition in part because they symbolize purity and fertility, and brides in Victorian times often wore them in their hair.

holidays.name: National Indige-Nerd Day
holidays.description: A day for Indigenous people and allies to celebrate the nerdy things they love, including comics, gaming, sci-fi, anime, and fandoms, all while promoting Indigenous representation in geek culture.
holidays.origin: The observance began in 2019 on social media as an effort to highlight Indigenous creators and fans in pop culture spaces.
holidays.funFact: The hashtag lets fans share art, cosplay, and stories, helping to counter stereotypes that Indigenous cultures belong only in the past.

holidays.name: Helen Keller Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the life and achievements of Helen Keller, who became an author, activist, and lecturer despite being deaf and blind. It is a time to promote accessibility and awareness.
holidays.origin: Helen Keller was born on June 27, 1880, in Tuscumbia, Alabama. The day was recognized officially by a presidential proclamation in 1980 for the 100th anniversary of her birth.
holidays.funFact: Helen Keller was the first deaf and blind person to earn a Bachelor of Arts degree, graduating from Radcliffe College in 1904.

holidays.name: Global Wellness Day Eve Snack: National Indian Pudding Day
holidays.description: A day to dig into a warm, spoon-friendly dessert made from cornmeal, milk, molasses, and spices. It is a classic New England treat that is often served with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.
holidays.origin: Indian pudding came from early colonial settlers in New England, who adapted English hasty pudding using cornmeal, which was called Indian meal at the time.
holidays.funFact: The name has nothing to do with India. Colonists used the term Indian meal for cornmeal, and the pudding kept the name.
